## Package layout

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `R/ingest.R` | Data sources, parquet import/export, data contract |
| `R/preprocess.R` | Pre-processing per dataset (from the templates) |
| `R/ae_dictionary.R` | Readable adverse event names |
| `R/cm_dictionary.R` | Real medication names and ATC classes for ADCM |
| `R/data_pipeline.R` | `load_blockr_data()`: pipeline + caches |
| `R/teal_data.R` | `teal_data` object, reproducible code, join keys |
| `R/blocks_graph.R` | Block graphs: R code to a graph of blocks, dependencies |
| `R/blocks_compile.R` | Block graphs to R code (clean and block-by-block), formatting |
| `R/blocks_run.R` | Running a graph block by block: cache, status of each block, column lists |
| `R/blocks_registry.R` | The blocks the canvas knows: names, help, summaries, editors |
| `R/blocks_sas.R` | Block graphs as SAS code (a translation; TODO for the rest) |
| `R/canvas.R` | The canvas module (home page): UI, server, messages with the browser |
| `R/app_modules.R` | Module configuration (one function per tab group) |
| `R/app_filters.R` | Module-specific filters / starting populations |
| `R/app_ui.R` | Header (logo, data badge, dark mode toggle), footer, favicon, asset dependency |
| `R/plot_theme.R` | Plot defaults: `teal.ggplot2_args`, default ggplot2 theme of the plot modules |
| `R/tlg_catalog.R` | TLG Catalog module: registry, page, runner, renderers |
| `R/tlg_entries_*.R` | TLG Catalog outputs (one function per topic group) |
| `R/run_app.R` | `blockr_app()`, `run_app()` |
| `R/options.R` | `?blockr_options` |
| `inst/www/` | Stylesheets, scripts (the canvas editor, colour mode, TLG Catalog list), logo, favicon and fonts |
| `inst/templates/` | The original teal.gallery templates |
| `app.R` | Launcher for RStudio "Run App" / Posit Connect |

## Everyday workflow

```{r}
devtools::load_all()   # load the package from source
run_app()

devtools::document()   # regenerate man/ and NAMESPACE from roxygen comments
devtools::test()       # run the test suite
devtools::check()      # full R CMD check
```

## Adding or changing a module

Modules live in `R/app_modules.R`, in the function of their tab group
(`modules_exploratory()`, `modules_safety()`). Keep labels unique across the
app: module-specific filters are keyed by label, and `blockr_modules()` stops
if two modules share one. Safety modules automatically get their starting
population (see `R/app_filters.R`).

Exploratory plot modules are created with
`blockr_plot_module(tm_g_..., <arguments>)` rather than a direct call: it
adds the app's default ggplot2 theme (option `blockr.ggtheme`), but only when
the installed module version has a matching theme argument, so a module API
change cannot break the app.

If a new module needs a dataset column that is not yet in the contract, add it
to `adam_contract()`; if it pre-selects a value, add it to
`adam_app_defaults()`.

## Adding or changing a TLG Catalog output

Each output is one `tlg()` entry in `R/tlg_entries_*.R`:

```{r}
tlg("AET02", "Adverse Events", "Table",
    topic = "Adverse Events", slug = "adverse-events",
    data = c("ADSL", "ADAE"),            # app datasets the code uses
    code = r"--(
library(tern)
adsl <- ADSL %>% filter(SAFFL == "Y") %>% df_explicit_na()
...
result <- build_table(lyt, df = adae, alt_counts_df = adsl)
)--")
```

The code is a plain string: it runs with teal's `eval_code()` on the page's
filtered data (datasets in upper case: `ADSL`, `ADAE`, ...) and must create
`result`: an rtables table, an rlistings listing, a data.frame, or a plot
(ggplot2, grid or lattice). The same string is what "Show R code" shows. Use
`BlockR::tlg_example_data("ADPC", adsl)` (and list the dataset in `extra`)
for datasets the app does not load; list non-default packages in `packages`.

`test-tlg-catalog.R` renders every output on the bundled data and lists the
ones that fail with their error message (skip it with
`Sys.setenv(BLOCKR_SKIP_TLG = "true")`).

## The canvas

### Graphs of blocks

The canvas edits a *graph*: a plain list that travels as JSON between R and
the browser (its fields are documented at the top of `R/blocks_graph.R`).
Each node is a block: a dataset, a function call (`fn` and `args`, each
argument R code or a reference to another block), an R expression or an R
statement. A block can take the block above it as its `input` (a pipe step,
or a ggplot2 layer added with `+`) and may be assigned to a variable (`name`).

```{r}
g <- blockr_graph_from_code(tlg_catalog()$AET02$code)
cat(blockr_compile(g)$code)           # the same code again
steps <- blockr_compile(g, "debug")   # one statement per block
```

Three rules keep code and blocks in step:

* a pipe chain becomes a stack of blocks, and blocks stacked on top of each
  other become a pipe chain again, assigned to the variable of its last named
  block (a named block ends its chain, so the template's variables are kept);
* a variable used as a whole argument becomes a wire (`ref`); inside a larger
  expression it is an *implicit* dependency (`blockr_graph_deps()`), resolved
  to the last assignment before the block;
* statements run in dependency order, ties in the order of the original
  code, so an unedited template runs exactly as written.

`blockr_run()` evaluates the "debug" form block by block in an environment
holding the datasets, and caches each block's value under a key made of its
code and the keys of the blocks it depends on; the canvas empties the cache
when the filtered data change. It returns the status of every block: its
state (`ok`, `error`, `blocked`, `missing`), what it produced (`data`,
`listing`, `table`, `layout`, `plot`, `value`), its size, its columns (for
the column pickers, sent once per session) and its error.

### The editor

`inst/www/blockr_canvas.js` holds the graph in the browser. After every
change it sends the graph (without the positions) as `input$graph`; R answers
with the `blockr-status` message, and the Result and Block panels are
ordinary Shiny outputs. Other messages: `input$ready` -> `blockr-data` (the
datasets), `input$template` -> `blockr-graph` (a template's graph, with its
implicit dependencies for the first layout), `input$code` (R code, JSON with
`code`, `title` and `mode` "replace" or "add") -> `blockr-graph` (with `mode`
and `source = "code"`) or `blockr-code-error` (the parse error, by line),
`input$lang` ("r" / "sas": while it is "sas", R sends `blockr-sas` with the
SAS code after every run), `input$selected`, `input$show_code`. Every
message carries the canvas's namespace (`ns`), so the page's two canvases
(yours and the tutorial's) each get their own. The canvas is saved in the
browser's `localStorage`.

Pasted code added to a canvas (`Editor.prototype.addGraph`) gets new block
ids, reuses the datasets already on the canvas and renames variables that
clash (`adsl` -> `adsl_2`), also in the new blocks' code after the block that
defines them (before it, the name still means the canvas's variable).

### SAS code

`blockr_sas(graph, status = run$status)` writes the graph as SAS, chain by
chain (`blockr_compile()`'s `chains`): the row-wise steps of a stack make one
DATA step, order / unique rows a PROC SORT, count / summarise / joins PROC
SQL; a table layout stack is read as columns, total column, row groups and
analyses (`sas_layout()`), and Build table becomes PROC SQL / MEANS steps on
the rows stacked once more for the total column, with N from the
column-count data (`sas_table()`); listings become PROC REPORT, ggplot2
stacks PROC SGPLOT / SGPANEL, `g_km()` PROC LIFETEST. R expressions are
translated by `sas_expr()` (comparisons, `%in%`, `is.na`, `ifelse`,
`paste`, `substr`, ...); `case_when()` and `cut()` become SELECT / WHEN.
Anything else is kept as a TODO comment with its R code. The run's column
types (`status`) tell numbers from categories (PROC MEANS or counts). To
translate one more function, add it to `sas_expr()` (an expression),
`sas_steps()` (a data step) or `sas_layout()` (a layout block), and a case
to `tests/testthat/test-sas.R`.

A block is drawn under its input when it is the only block using that input;
otherwise it starts a stack of its own, with a wire. The output of a stack is
its last block: a block added at the bottom takes over the stack's wires and
variable, and deleting a block hands them back to the block above.

### Adding a block to the palette

Add a `bk_block()` entry to `R/blocks_registry.R`:

```{r}
bk_block(
  "slice_head", "First rows", "prep", input = TRUE, palette = TRUE,
  help = "Keeps the first rows (of each group).",
  summary = "Keep the first {n} rows",
  formals = c(".data", "...", "n", "prop", "by"),
  args = list(bk_arg("n", "Rows", "number", main = TRUE)),
  insert = bk_insert(n = "5")
)
```

* `input = TRUE`: the block works on the result of the block above it;
  `op = "+"` for ggplot2 layers.
* `formals` lets the editor recognise unnamed arguments (the piped input
  takes the first one).
* `summary` is the line shown on the block: `{n}` is the argument's value
  (or a red "…" when it is missing), `{?n}` the value if there is one,
  `{n?text}` / `{n?!text}` a text shown only when `n` is set / not set,
  `{...}` the unnamed arguments.
* Editors: `column`, `columns`, `symbols`, `conditions`, `assign`, `labels`,
  `text`, `number`, `bool`, `choice`, `strings`, `named`, `aes`, `data`,
  `code` (see the top of the file).
* `insert`: the settings of a new block taken from the palette.

Templates need no registry entry: any function is a block, and its settings
are edited as R code. `test-blocks.R` checks that every palette block
compiles and that every template compiles without problems.

### The tutorial

The canvas page (`tm_blockr_canvas()`) holds two canvases: the user's
(`main`) and the tutorial's (`tutorial`), each with its own server
(`srv_blockr_canvas_app()`) and saved state; the Tutorial button switches the
views (`showView()` in `blockr_canvas.js`). The tutorial's canvas has
`tutorial: true` in its configuration, so the editor attaches
`inst/www/blockr_tutorial.js` to it. The module turns teal's report and code
buttons off (`blockr_without_teal_buttons()`, with teal's `disable_report()`
/ `disable_src()` when available); if teal still draws them, the browser
hides them and puts the Tutorial button there (`dockTutorial()`). The editor emits events
(`change`, `status`, `graph`, `select`, `pane`, `tip`, `connected`; see
`Editor.prototype.on`) and the tutorial re-checks the current step on each.

A lesson is data:

```js
{
  id: "filter", level: 0, title: "Keep only some rows",
  intro: "...",
  start: { graph: [{ dataset: "ADSL" }], title: "..." },  // or { code: "R code" }, { template: "AET02" }
  steps: [{
    text: "Add <b>Filter rows</b> below ADSL ...",
    check: function (q) { return q.calls("filter").some(function (n) { return q.below(n, "ADSL"); }); },
    show: palette('data-fn="filter"'),                      // what "Show me" points at
    hint: "..."
  }]
}
```

Checks ask questions about the canvas (`q.calls(fn)`, `q.dataset(name)`,
`q.below(block, dataset)`, `q.hasCond(block, col, op, value)`,
`q.arg(block, formal)`, `q.dotsSymbols(block)`, `q.selected()`,
`q.did("pane" | "tip" | "select", test)` for what happened since the step
started, `q.memo()` for a step that needs two moments). `test-canvas.R`
checks that every lesson starts from valid R code and existing templates.

## Styling and the interactive layer

The look lives in `inst/www/blockr.css` and the behaviour in
`inst/www/blockr.js` (no dependencies). `inst/www/tlg_catalog.css` holds
the layout of the TLG Catalog pages only (Bootstrap variables, no colours of
its own); `blockr.css` skins those pages in its last section.

The stylesheet redefines Bootstrap's CSS variables on top of teal's default
theme instead of compiling a custom `bslib::bs_theme()`. That keeps bslib's
precompiled CSS (no Sass compilation at start-up) and the app recognisably
teal. Its tokens (`--tn-*`: type scale, spacing, radii, motion, canvas,
panels, lines, ink levels, accent and signal colours) are defined once for
both modes and per mode in the `html:not([data-bs-theme="dark"])` (light) and
`html[data-bs-theme="dark"]` blocks. Appearance settings are attributes on
`<html>` that override tokens (`data-tn-text`, `data-tn-density`,
`data-tn-accent`, `data-tn-corners`, `data-tn-contrast`, `data-tn-canvas`);
the current category is `data-tn-section` (set by the script), which picks
the accent tokens of that category unless a fixed accent is chosen. Guidelines:

* prefer changing a token or a `--bs-*` variable over styling a component;
* dark-mode values go in the `html[data-bs-theme="dark"]` block;
* selectors start with `html` when they must win over widget stylesheets that
  load later (e.g. ionRangeSlider, selectize);
* keep drawing cheap: no `backdrop-filter`, no background images, no
  infinite animations; animate `transform`, `opacity` and colours only;
* entrance animations use `backwards` fill (or end on `none`), so no
  `transform` is left on a surface afterwards;
* never set a font family inside plots (see `R/plot_theme.R`).

`blockr.js` works from the page itself, so it does not depend on how teal
builds its navigation:

* **Navigation model**: every Bootstrap tab trigger (`data-bs-toggle="tab"`
  or `"pill"`) and its chain of parent tabs and menus gives the path of a
  view. Opening a view shows each tab of its chain in turn (Bootstrap's Tab
  API). Elements that are not Bootstrap tabs are reached by clicking the
  visible elements labelled with each part of the path.
* **Index**: the header carries a JSON index (`blockr_index()` in
  `R/app_ui.R`): the path and kind of every module and the ID, title, type and
  topic of every TLG output. The command bar uses it for order, icons and the
  outputs; without it, it indexes the tabs it finds.
* **Views** are tracked from Bootstrap's `shown.bs.tab` events and clicks on
  tabs and TLG outputs; each view updates the breadcrumb, the page title, the
  address (`history.pushState`, a `#/` path of slugs) and the recent list
  (`localStorage`). On load and on `popstate`, the `#/` path is opened.
* **Status** uses Shiny's `shiny:busy` / `shiny:idle` events.
* **Home page**: the canvas (kind `canvas` in the index); `H` and the logo
  go there.
* **Tools and pins** work on `.shiny-plot-output img` and on HTML tables
  outside DataTables; pins are kept in memory for the session (images as data
  URLs, tables as HTML).
* Settings from R (`blockr.color_mode`, `blockr.motion`) arrive in
  `window.blockr` through the inline script of the header dependency,
  which also applies dark mode and the saved appearance before the first
  paint.
* **Start-up**: `blockr_app()` keeps the built app in `the$app_cache`
  (keyed by `blockr_app_key()`: package version, data signature, look
  options); `run_app()` wraps teal's UI with `blockr_fast_ui()`, which
  serves the first page built for a plain request again. `tlg_catalog()` is
  memoised. The build message breaks the time down by step.

### Fonts

The fonts are subsets converted to WOFF2 with
[fontTools](https://github.com/fonttools/fonttools): Inter (the variable
font, pinned to its text optical size; every weight) and JetBrains Mono
(no-ligature cut). To rebuild them (e.g. for a newer Inter release), keep
Latin, Greek, punctuation, arrows and mathematical operators:

```sh
UNICODES="U+0000-00FF,U+0100-017F,U+0131,U+0152-0153,U+02BB-02BC,U+02C6,U+02DA,U+02DC,U+0370-03FF,U+2000-206F,U+2070-209F,U+20AC,U+2122,U+2190-21FF,U+2200-22FF,U+2300-23FF,U+25A0-25FF,U+2713-2717,U+FEFF,U+FFFD"

fonttools varLib.instancer InterVariable.ttf opsz=14 -o inter-text.ttf
pyftsubset inter-text.ttf --flavor=woff2 --layout-features='*' --no-hinting \
  --desubroutinize --output-file=InterVariable.woff2 --unicodes="$UNICODES"
```

JetBrains Mono uses the same `pyftsubset` command on
`JetBrainsMonoNL-Regular.ttf` and `-Bold.ttf` (no instancer step; the
unicode list adds box drawing, `U+2500-257F`). Licences and copyright notices
are in `inst/www/fonts/OFL.txt` and `inst/COPYRIGHTS`.

## Tests

The suite (`tests/testthat/`) checks every step:

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| `test-ingest.R` | every source, synthetic settings and reproducibility, parquet naming and round trip |
| `test-contract.R` | each rule of the data contract on tiny hand-made data |
| `test-preprocess.R` | invariants of every derived dataset |
| `test-ae-dictionary.R` | AE decoding (one-to-one, unknown codes, labels kept) |
| `test-data-pipeline.R` | memory/disk/fresh caches, refresh, invalidation, global copies |
| `test-teal-data.R` | datasets, join keys, reproducible code, error messages |
| `test-app.R` | app builds without warnings, UI renders, labels, filter mapping, no third-party requests |
| `test-speed.R` | page cache, app cache key, memoised registry, cache clearing |
| `test-blocks.R` | block graphs: **every template round-trips** (code -> blocks -> code) and computes the same values block by block, compiling edited graphs, problems per block, formatting, the runner (sizes, errors, cache, packages, result), the registry, and (with tern) the canvas result of every template against the TLG Catalog's |
| `test-canvas.R` | the canvas page and its configuration, the graph from the browser, template graphs, status messages, outputs, the server on the app's data |
| `test-look.R` | assets and fonts, light and dark tokens, styles of the interactive layer, the script's wiring, options, header/footer, module index, icons, colour-mode script, plot defaults |
| `test-tlg-catalog.R` | TLG Catalog registry, page, runner, and **every output on the bundled data** |

**Consistency whatever the data.** The data invariants run on several
*different* datasets - the bundled data, two synthetic draws of different size
and seed, and a parquet round trip - so they test properties of the pipeline,
not one snapshot. Run a subset with an environment variable:

```{r}
Sys.setenv(BLOCKR_TEST_SCENARIOS = "bundled")   # quick run
devtools::test()
```

The parquet tests need *arrow* and are skipped without it. Tests use temporary
cache folders and a throw-away memory cache; they never touch your real cache
or Global Environment.

## Deployment

`app.R` at the project root loads the package with `pkgload::load_all()` and
calls `run_app()`, so the project folder can be deployed as a Shiny app
(e.g. `rsconnect::deployApp()`). `R/_disable_autoload.R` stops Shiny from also
sourcing `R/` on its own.
